tasks.short: Read orders and blueprints to determine forging setup requirements

steps.what: Locate current work orders and blueprint revisions
Read blueprints and work orders for specified tolerances
Determine setup sequence and resolve conflicting specifications
outputs: determined setup requirements and unresolved questions

steps.what: Write working setup notes and source revision references
inputs: determined setup requirements and unresolved questions

tasks.design: Configure a current-job drawing view in {OPS_SYSTEM} and linked working-note headings in {DOCS}. The setter reads tolerances and decides the setup sequence personally; the actual work-note writing is separately priced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current revisions and repeated source details are located and copied into setup notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Native job links and note fields may reduce source and record handling.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting tolerances and recognising conflicting or incomplete setup requirements.
tasks.human_edge: Practical machine knowledge and careful drawing interpretation.
tasks.altitude: Less reference administration before the physical setup.

reach.task: Trace setup requirements to a drawing revision
reach.learn: Keep the applicable source visible beside working notes

evidence.claim: Native current-job views and linked notes may reduce repeated handling; the digest provides no forging blueprint-interpretation time case.

assumptions: Scenario includes existing setup work notes where written today; verify that baseline rather than creating a new record. Physical setup is separately priced in10088.

Engineering produces the controlled drawing and planning produces the work order, with their source creation time owned by those tasks. Setter verifies job, part, drawing revision, units and applicable requirements in s1-s3 and writes source references and work points in s4; all focal capture is counted. Missing or conflicting revisions require manual clarification.
Native current-job views and note structures come first; no model reads tolerances into machine settings or chooses the operation sequence.
Ordinary same-system saves stay fully retained within s4 and have no self-approval stage.
unknowns: Whether setup work notes are written
research_questions: Do native links reduce lookup and note entry without presenting an obsolete drawing as current?

incremental.description: Maintain job links and note fields

tasks.short: Confer with colleagues on forging setups and specifications

steps.what: Retrieve current setup and operational specifications for discussion
Confer with other workers and clarify setup or specification issues
outputs: clarified setup points and unresolved issues

steps.what: Write setup discussion notes and agreed follow-up points
inputs: clarified setup points and unresolved issues

tasks.design: Configure current specification links in {OPS_SYSTEM} and concise discussion-note fields in {DOCS}. The colleague conversation and judgement stay human; writing actual setup notes remains a distinct task step.
tasks.previous_blocker: References and recurring discussion-note headings require repeated handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and fields can reduce supporting lookup and writing.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding practical observations and resolving unclear or conflicting setup information.
tasks.human_edge: Shared shop-floor experience and precise clarification.
tasks.altitude: Reduce supporting record effort around the human exchange.

reach.learn: Distinguish agreed points from unresolved technical questions

evidence.claim: Native reference and note configuration may reduce clerical work around a setup discussion; no measured case is provided in the digest.

assumptions: Includes the existing discussion record where made today. Do not count the same setup work note again if this discussion is part of10079; allocate the actual episode once.

Setter captures the question and current specification reference in s1, produces clarified points in s2 and records job, revision, agreed point and unresolved issue in s3. All capture time is counted; missing references and disputed points are clarified manually.
Native source links and short note fields come first. No model selects a setup, changes a machine or performs an implied send.
Communication is internal; the author saves the record without an extra approval stage and its save time stays fully retained.
unknowns: Whether discussion notes are written and where
research_questions: Can reference and note configuration reduce handling without turning an unresolved issue into an apparent agreement?

incremental.description: Maintain discussion links and note fields

approvals.approved_version: Exact setup point and current specification reference communicated to colleagues; changed or uncertain points require renewed clarification

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R93 gross7 less1 upkeep gives central6. Low retains all10 lookup and24/25 note writing when a novel exception requires detailed explanation: gross1 less1=0. High retains9/10 lookup and22/25 notes when current links and concise agreed-point fields fit: gross4 less1=3. The actual colleague discussion remains full.

tasks.short: Select, align and secure forging fixtures and dies

steps.what: Look up specified fixtures, stops and dies for this setup
Select physical tooling and check its suitability and identity
Align positioning fixtures, stops and specified dies
Bolt tooling to the machine and check the physical installation
Record installed fixture and die identifiers in the setup record

tasks.design: Configure native tooling-register links in {OPS_SYSTEM} and existing installation-record fields in {DOCS}. Selection, alignment and physical securing remain human; tooling lookup and the actual installation record are priced separately from the physical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tooling identifiers are located and written repeatedly around a hands-on setup.
tasks.enabler_now: Native register views and record fields may reduce small amounts of supporting handling.
tasks.still_hard: Physical tooling suitability, alignment and secure installation on the actual machine.
tasks.human_edge: Practical skill and direct inspection of the installation.
tasks.altitude: Simplify the supporting record while retaining physical setup expertise.

reach.learn: Keep the register reference tied to the physical tool

evidence.claim: Native tooling links and installation records may reduce clerical handling; the digest's machine-monitoring products do not perform physical die alignment or installation.

assumptions: Scenario includes existing installed-tool identification recording, not a new sign-off invented to create saving. Measure whether that record exists and keep physical work full.

Engineering and tooling staff produce controlled requirements and register entries during their own source-maintenance work. Setter captures required tool identifier and revision in s1, verifies the physical item in s2, and records actual installed identifiers, job and date in s5. All focal capture is counted; missing or mismatched identifiers require manual resolution.
Native tooling views and existing record fields come first; no structured ready flag, automatic setup, machine adjustment or implied notification is assumed.

Same-system author saves remain fully retained within s5 with no extra approval. Working requirement notes under10079 and actual installed-tool records here are distinct; allocate any shared record once.
unknowns: Whether actual installed-tool identifiers are recorded
Tooling-register quality and current native views
Division of setup and quality-record responsibilities
research_questions: Can native tooling links reduce identifier handling without confusing a register entry with the physically installed tool?
